name: Bibha Chowdhuri
summary: Indian particle physicist and pioneer in cosmic ray research using photographic nuclear emulsions.

name: D. M. Bose
summary: Physicist and director of the Bose Institute, mentor and cousin-in-law to Bibha Chowdhuri.

name: Cecil Powell
summary: Nobel laureate physicist who acknowledged Chowdhuri's pioneering efforts in meson research.

name: P. M. S. Blackett
summary: Nobel laureate physicist under whom Chowdhuri worked at the University of Manchester.

name: Homi Bhabha
summary: Physicist who recruited Chowdhuri to the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

name: Vikram Sarabhai
summary: Leader of the Physical Research Laboratory where Chowdhuri worked on cosmic-ray research.

name: Bose Institute
summary: Research institute in Kolkata where Chowdhuri began her career.

name: University of Calcutta
summary: University where Chowdhuri completed her B.Sc, M.Sc, and teaching faculty role.

name: University of Manchester
summary: University where Chowdhuri completed her PhD under Patrick Blackett.

name: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research
summary: Research institute where Chowdhuri was the first female researcher.

name: Physical Research Laboratory
summary: Laboratory in Ahmedabad where Chowdhuri worked under Vikram Sarabhai.

name: Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics
summary: Institute where Chowdhuri collaborated in later years.

name: International Astronomical Union
summary: Organization which named a star in Chowdhuri's honour.

name: Kolkata
summary: City in West Bengal, India, where Chowdhuri was born and spent much of her life.

name: Manchester

name: Ahmedabad

name: Bibha
summary: Star named by the IAU in honour of Chowdhuri.
